"name": "Coordinating complexity: Delivering global diagnostic imaging studies across modalities and patient populations",
"description": "This case study highlights how Fortrea successfully delivered complex global diagnostic imaging studies across multiple imaging modalities, patient populations, therapeutic areas, and international locations. Diagnostic imaging research requires highly coordinated execution involving radiology, radiopharmacy, medical physics, surgery, laboratory services, and clinical operations teams working within strict procedural timelines. The study demonstrates how careful planning, patient pathway coordination, radiotracer manufacture and validation, imaging compliance measures, and cross-functional collaboration supported successful delivery despite operational complexity. Fortrea implemented structured site readiness strategies, imaging qualification processes, early validation activities, and multidisciplinary coordination to address challenges related to imaging protocol complexity, resource constraints, patient recruitment, retention, and site capacity limitations. The case study also highlights the importance of imaging standardization, radiotracer management, risk mitigation, and proactive engagement across study teams to support efficient and reliable study execution. By combining operational expertise with a structured approach to patient pathways, site readiness, and imaging workflows, Fortrea enabled the successful delivery of high-quality imaging data across PET, CT, SPECT, MRI, ultrasound, ECG-based imaging, and theranostic imaging studies. The outcome demonstrates how early planning, collaboration, and operational excellence can improve study readiness, support protocol adherence, and ensure successful global diagnostic imaging study delivery."
